penalties.impact: Rs.9,77,040/- each. HCL, being a Government Company, the power of appointment of directors on its Board as per its Articles of Association is vested with President of India, acting through the Ministry of Mines, Government of India. The Company has written to the Ministry of Mines, Government of India for appointment of required number of directors on the Board of HCL and the matter is under consideration. Consequent upon appointment of required number of directors on the Board of HCL, the Company will seek waiver of fines from both BSE and NSE. tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: In Maharashtra prior to 2017, Octroi charge was levied for inward material but from 01.01.2017 Octroi was abolished and Local Body Tax (LBT) was levied. In Taloja Copper Project (TCP) of Hindustan Copper Ltd. (HCL), LBT charge was levied on the value of Cathode received at TCP from 01.01.2017 to 31.03.2017 and 01.04.2017 to 30.06.2017. The demand is of approx. Rs.58 crore. Status as per Last Disclosure: The matter has still not been heard. A stay for same dispute filed by the Taloja Manufacturing Association, of which TCP, HCL is a part, has already been granted by High court. The case will be combined with other similar case and will be taken up for hearing. Next date of hearing is awaited.
tax_litigation.status: The matter has still not been heard. A stay for same dispute filed by the Taloja Manufacturing Association, of which TCP, HCL is a part, has already been granted by High Court. The case will be combined with other similar case and will be taken up for hearing. Next hearing date is 23.01.2026.

tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: Malanjkhand Copper Project (MCP), a unit of Hindustan Copper Limited filed Case No. MJC 1 of 2016 before the Civil Court, Baihar challenging notice dated 18.01.2007 received from the Municipal Council, Malanjkhand demanding a sum of Rs.74.87 crore against Terminal Tax with 10 times penalty for the period 2000-2006. MCP has deposited Rs.19 crore (approximately) as per self-assessment and in compliance with Orders of the Courts in the account of Municipal Council, Malajkhand. Status as per Last Disclosure: Vide final judgment dated 28.07.2025, the Civil Court, Baihar rejected HCL/MCP’s appeal. On 07.05.2025, HCL filed an application before the Additional Secretary (FA), Ministry of Mines, Government of India, and subsequently vide letter dated 16.05.2025 to Deputy Secretary (FA), Ministry of Mines, Government of India, under the Administrative Mechanism for Resolution of CPSE’s Disputes (AMRCD) mechanism to get relief. The matter is pending under AMRCD.
tax_litigation.opposing_party: Case. No. MJC 1 of 2016, Civil Court, Baihar Hindustan Copper Limited, Malanjkhand Copper Project Vs. Municipal Council, Malanjkhand
tax_litigation.status: On 16.10.2025, HCL has filed a Revision Application before the Court of Additional District Judge, Baihar, praying for setting aside the Demand Bill dated 03.01.2007 issued by the Municipal Council, Malanjkhand; and the final judgment dated 28.07.2025 passed by the Civil Court, Baihar in Case No. MJC 01/2016. The matter is pending under AMRCD for Amicable Resolution.

tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: Malanjkhand Copper Project (MCP), a unit of Hindustan Copper Limited filed Special Leave Petition No. 14928 of 2014 before the Supreme Court of India challenging notice dated 31.10.2012 received from the Municipal Council, Malajkhand demanding a sum of Rs.188.68 crore against Terminal Tax with 10 times penalty for the period 2006-2012. Vide Order dated 17.02.2025 Special Leave Petition No. 14928 of 2014, the Supreme Court directed HCL to deposit 50% of Rs.188.68 crore within 8 weeks from 17.02.2025. The matter has been disposed of by the Supreme Court vide Order dated 17.02.2025. Subsequently, HCL/MCP filed a Miscellaneous Application No. 838 of 2025 in respect of Order dated 17.02.2025 passed by the Supreme Court in SLP (C) No. 14928 of 2014, praying for allowing HCL to deposit Rs. 5.3 crores, which is the difference of Terminal Tax calculated by the Municipal Council, i.e., Rs. 17,18,94,364/- and amount paid by HCL/MCP as per self-assessment, i.e., Rs. 11.88 crores. Vide Order dated 05.05.2025, the Supreme Court dismissed HCL/MCP's application On 07.05.2025, HCL filed an application before the Additional Secretary (FA), Ministry of Mines, Government of India, and subsequently vide letter dated 16.05.2025 to Deputy Secretary (FA), Ministry of Mines, Government of India, under the Administrative Mechanism for Resolution of CPSE's Disputes (AMRCD) mechanism to get relief. Status as per Last Disclosure: On 05.08.2025, Municipal Council Malanjkhand filed Contempt Petition (Civil) No. 628 of 2025 against Shri Nagesh Shenoy, ED & Unit Head, HCL/MCP for contempt of Order of the Hon’ble Supreme Court dated 17.02.2025 in SLP (C) No. 14928 of 2014. The hearing is 09.12.2025.
tax_litigation.opposing_party: Contempt Petition (Civil) No. 628 of 2025, Supreme Court Municipal Council , Malanjkhand Vs. Nagesh Shenoy
tax_litigation.status: HCL has filed reply in the matter during last hearing on 07.10.2025. The next date is fixed for 07.04.2026.

tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: Hindustan Copper Ltd had requested Subarnrekha Canal Division, Water Resource Department Ghatshila, Jharkhand to reassess its earlier demand of Rs.216 crore raised for consumption of natural river stream water from river Subranrekha at Jharkhand. The Department has considered request of HCL and vide its Letter dated 19.05.2026 (received on 27.05.2026), has conveyed that on the basis of the data provided by the Company and the departmental water rates issued from time to time, the total outstanding amount from the year 2005 to October, 2025 has been estimated at Rs.87.926 crore. The total outstanding amount from the year 2000-01 to 2005 was Rs.4.247 crore, adding which the total outstanding amount till date has been estimated at Rs.92.166 crore (Water charges Rs.46.623 crore and Penalty of Rs.45.543 crore). The estimated outstanding water tax bill has been provided to Hindustan Copper Ltd for confirmation. The Company is evaluating the calculation made by the Water Resource Department Ghatshila, Jharkhand.
tax_litigation.opposing_party: 1) State Of Jharkhand 2) Secretary, Deptt Of Water Resources (Earlier Known As Irrigation Deptt) 3) Superintending Engineer, Baraj Circle, Subarnrekha Project, Deptt Of Water Resources 4) Executive Engineer, Subarnrekha Canal Division, Deptt Of Water Resources
tax_litigation.status: HCL has challenged the demand notice of water resource dept. over consumption of natural river stream water from river Subranrekha at Jharkhand High court. Discuss with Water Resource Department regarding out of court settlement due to non-notification by state government. Case is pending at the admission stage, next date of hearing is 01.09.2026.

industry: Commodities > Metals & Mining > Non - Ferrous Metals > Copper

operating_notes.text: Q1FY27 consolidated revenue of ₹936.5 Cr was 19% below Q4FY26's ₹1,156.08 Cr, the highest quarter in memory.
Changes in inventories were a ₹37.21 Cr credit in Q1FY27, continuing the drawdown seen in Q1FY26 (-₹30.72 Cr).
The company operates as a single segment (copper ore mining and processing through continuous copper wire rods) under Ind AS 108.
FY27 ore production target raised to 5.90 MTPA, up 26% YoY from 4.71 MTPA
5-year roadmap targets 12.20 MTPA ore production by FY29-30
Malanjkhand expansion to 5.00 MTPA, Khetri concentrator to 3.00 MTPA
BSE and NSE each fined ₹14,43,140 (₹12,23,000 plus 18% GST) for the June 2026 quarter over board composition and audit, NRC, stakeholder and risk committee constitution.
Hind Copper plans ₹7,000 Cr capex over 5-6 years for mine expansion
Hind Copper targets 12.20 MTPA ore production by FY29-30
Hind Copper to expand Malanjkhand to 5.00 MTPA and Khetri to 3.00 MTPA by FY30
Jabalpur Commercial Court stayed an arbitration award against HCL on condition of a 50% bank guarantee and a 50% asset-valuation bond; Section 34 challenge to be heard after deposit.
ICRA upgraded HCL's long-term rating to [ICRA]AAA (Stable) from [ICRA]AA+ (Stable) and reaffirmed short-term [ICRA]A1+ on ₹2,200 Cr total facilities (₹2,100 Cr bank facilities + ₹100 Cr CP).
